diagnostic_evidence.quote: Maximizing this bound over $ 0 < \eps \leq 1 $ gives the optimal balance $ \eps^7 \sim \tau^2, \eps^5\sim h^2 $, leading to a uniform accuracy of $ O\big( \tau^{2/7} + h^{2/5} \big) $ in the maximum norm for all $ 0 < \eps \leq 1 $. The optimal quadratic convergence rate is achieved when $\eps\sim 1$ or $\eps\leq \tau^2+h^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract presents second-order accuracy together with uniform convergence across the full parameter range, whereas the paper's own optimization gives only the uniform rates $\tau^{2/7}$ and $h^{2/5}$. Quadratic convergence is explicitly restricted to special regimes, so it is not a uniform second-order guarantee.

failure_location.quote: Both methods achieve second-order accuracy with time steps and mesh sizes that are not restricted in magnitude by~$\eps$. The methods are uniformly convergent in the range from arbitrarily small to moderately bounded $\eps$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the second-order claim to the parameter regimes where the paper establishes it and state the lower $O(\tau^{2/7}+h^{2/5})$ rate for uniform convergence over $0<\eps\le1$.
issues.overall_effect: The headline description materially overstates the uniform convergence order established by the paper.
issues.title: Advertised uniform second-order accuracy contradicts the stated uniform rates
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws a central advertised guarantee—uniform second-order accuracy—and replaces it by materially lower uniform rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The $BC^1(\R)$-norm is stronger than the norm of the Wiener algebra $A(\R)$, as is implied by \eqref{eq:katz}. Hence, the $\mathcal{O}(\eps)$ defect bound is also valid in the $A(\R)$-norm.
The proof is based on \eqref{eq:katz} and follows the same steps as the proof in \cite[Lemma 4.2]{shi2025weighted}.

issues.failure_explanation: No universal bound of the Wiener norm by only the sup norms of a function and its first derivative holds on $\mathbb R$. For example, sums of increasingly many disjoint translates of one fixed smooth compactly supported bump have uniformly bounded function and derivative sup norms, while their Fourier $L^1$ norms are unbounded. Thus the asserted implication from a $BC^1$ defect bound to an $A(\mathbb R)$ defect bound is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false embedding by valid spatial integrability or Sobolev/Wiener assumptions and prove that the exact envelopes, correctors, and defects satisfy uniform bounds in those stronger norms.
issues.overall_effect: The Wiener-algebra bounds used for the continuous approximations and numerical consistency are not established under the stated bounded-derivative assumptions, so the subsequent uniform error arguments lack a required input.
issues.title: False embedding of bounded $C^1$ functions into the Wiener algebra
issues.why_classification: A comparable result may survive after strengthening regularity and decay hypotheses, but this requires new norm estimates rather than a local algebraic correction.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify consistent one-sided or exact initial velocity formulas and either compute one extra time level or use a terminal one-sided reconstruction, with a local accuracy check.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\mathcal{I}$ is an interpolation operator ensuring a smooth transition in the overlapping region.

issues.failure_explanation: At a physical point $x_i$, relation \eqref{eq:upq} requires evaluating $p$ at $x_i-c_gt_n/\eps$ and $q$ at $x_i+c_gt_n/\eps$. The displayed reconstruction instead interpolates both data sets at $x_i$, without specifying shifted interpolation nodes. Moreover, an operator described only as ensuring a smooth transition has no stated approximation order, so the claimed $O(h^2)$ reconstruction error does not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define interpolation of the envelopes or packet values on the correctly shifted physical grids, prescribe an interpolation operator of sufficient order, and bound its error uniformly through the overlap transition.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm does not unambiguously reconstruct the physical solution, and the general-data maximum-norm error theorem cannot follow directly from it.
issues.title: Global reconstruction omits the moving-coordinate shifts and leaves interpolation unspecified
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a concrete reconstruction and a contained but nontrivial interpolation-error argument; it need not alter the underlying packet schemes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Following the same procedure as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:stability} yields the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: The CFL condition does not provide a parameter-independent spectral separation. Taking a Fourier frequency with $\beta-\theta h=0$ gives $\widetilde\gamma_\theta=1$ and $\gamma_\theta=\alpha(1+\kappa^2)$. As $\tau\to0$, hence $\alpha\to0$, the ratio $\widetilde\gamma_\theta^2/(1+\gamma_\theta^2)$ tends to one. The two eigenvalues and the columns of $V(\theta)$ coalesce, so $\|V(\theta)^{-1}\|$ is unbounded. Thus no uniform $\mu<1$ follows, and the constructed norm is not uniformly equivalent to the product Wiener norm. The Crank--Nicolson proof repeats the same diagonalization and has the same small-step degeneracy.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the ill-conditioned eigenvector norm by a genuinely uniform energy or propagator estimate and redo the forced nonlinear stability analysis for both schemes.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform linear stability constants, the nonlinear Gronwall estimate, and consequently all stated parameter-uniform numerical error bounds are unsupported.
issues.title: Fourier diagonalization does not yield a uniformly equivalent stability norm
issues.why_classification: The existing stability architecture fails in the ordinary small-step limit, and all central uniform convergence theorems depend on it; a new stability argument is required.
